verdict.rationale: PayPal's Store Sync catalog feed spec documents exactly the machine-readable offer fields the story asks for — id, title, link (checkout URL), image_link, description, price, availability, with each row representing a distinct product variant — and getcart/createcart return live cart totals and payment state. However this is a merchant-published feed rather than an open discovery API any developer can query for arbitrary listed products: it's gated behind a manual access-approval form, scoped only to US-based physical goods in USD, and requires the merchant to already integrate Orders v2/Braintree. Missing for 10: a self-serve, unrestricted product-discovery endpoint/API (not just a feed spec) covering any listed product across merchants, digital goods/subscriptions, and non-US markets.
